svg.title: How to read Kern Fig. 17: caloric temperature factor F_c
svg.text: How to read Kern Fig. 17: caloric temperature factor F_c
Redrawn from Kern’s caloric equation F_c = (1/K_c + r/(r−1))/(1 + ln(K_c+1)/ln r) − 1/K_c, r = Δt_c/Δt_h
Get K_c (from °API and T₁ − T₂, upper part of Kern Fig. 17; example 0.4). Mark Δt_c/Δt_h (example 0.3).
Go straight up to the K_c curve (interpolate between curves if needed).
Go across to the F_c axis on the left.
Read F_c ≈ 0.37: T_c = T₂ + F_c(T₁ − T₂), t_c = t₁ + F_c(t₂ − t₁); properties are then taken at T_c, t_c.
For low-viscosity streams (water, light liquids) Kern uses the arithmetic mean temperatures instead.
Redrawn from the correlation; in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
Only the F_c part is redrawn; the K_c-from-°API part of the printed chart is not reproduced.
